newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 31.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Irish press on Thursday:
- The IRA will almost certainly have to hand over some of its arsenal early in the next phase of multi-party talks on a North peace pact, political sources revealed.
- Two men were swept to their deaths and two women were dramatically rescued in a fishing tragedy off Valentia Island.
- Up to 250,000 women who leave employment to raise or care for a family are to benefit from a new pensions deal.
- Another hectic day on the Dublin foreign exchange market saw up to 500 million traded as the pound remained the focus of attention for overseas traders.
- The Blood Transfusion Board has confirmed it is contacting up to 500 women who received potentially contaminated doses of anti-D in the 1970s, asking them to come forward for testing.

- Israel has suspended all peace talks with the Palestinian Authority and is demanding that Yasser Arafat launch an all-out assault on Islamic extremists after two Hamas suicide bombers killed 13 Israelis and left many more fighting for their lives in an attack yesterday.
- The abolition of the duty free market for EU citizens travelling within member states would isolate Ireland from Europe, a study said yesterday.
- Two men drowned and two women had a miraculous escape when they were swept off a rock by a freak wave while fishing at Valentia, County Kerry, yesterday.
- Education minister Micheal Martin was last night accused of attempting to re-introduce third level college fees by stealth.
